messages.content: What is the current time in New York City?

function.name: weather_forecast_get
function.description: Retrieve the current weather forecast for a specific location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location you want to retrieve the weather for.

hour.description: The hour of the day in 24-hour format (optional). If not provided, the current hour will be used. Default: 24

message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data, so I can’t give you the exact current time right now.  
New York City is in the Eastern Time Zone (UTC‑4 during daylight‑saving time, which is in effect in late July).  
If you need the precise time, you can check a world‑clock app, your phone’s clock, or a quick web search for “current time in New York.”

But we need to be careful: New York City is in Eastern Time Zone, which is UTC-5 during standard time, UTC-4 during daylight saving time. As of July 27, 2026, DST is likely in effect (DST in US runs from second Sunday in March to first Sunday in November). So it's UTC-4. We need to get current UTC time. But we don't have real-time. We could approximate by saying "I don't have real-time data" or we can use the system's time. But we can't access system time. We can approximate by saying "I don't have real-time data, but you can check your device." But maybe we can use the function to get weather forecast? No. There's no function for time.
